newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-ENTREPRENEUR SET TO COMPLETE STOUTE'S GOLDEN YEAR.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-ENTREPRENEUR SET TO COMPLETE STOUTE'S GOLDEN YEAR.

text.p: Entrepreneur is odds-on favourite to win Saturday's Epsom Derby and crown a fabulous 12 months for Newmarket trainer Michael Stoute.
Stoute's older horses Singspiel and Pilsudski have scored in an array of top international races, including the Breeders' Cup, The Japan Cup and the Dubai World Cup.
Entrepreneur won the 2,000 Guineas at Newmarket and now bids to join an elite group of horses, including Sir Ivor and Nijinsky, who have completed the Guineas/Derby double.
Stoute took the Derby with Shergar and Shahrastani in the 1980s so he knows what it needs. Jockey Michael Kinane, successful in 1993 on Commander-In-Chief, has a record second to none.

The only niggle is whether Entrepreneur can stay the 12-furlong (2.4-km) distance. There is a minor doubt on stamina in his breeding but the way the horse won the Guineas, running on strongly, suggests Saturday's distance will be within his scope.
If it is not, there are plenty waiting to unseat the 8-11 favourite, owned by bookmaker Michael Tabor.
Silver Patriarch leads the way, back down to 5-1 since his Derby trial success at Lingfield in May.
Trainer John Dunlop, seeking his third Derby winner, and veteran jockey Pat Eddery, chasing his fifth, are a solid combination but no grey horse has won the Derby since 1946.

Third favourite Benny The Dip (10-1) won the Dante Stakes at York under an excellent ride from Olivier Peslier but the Frenchman has deserted the horse. The capable but less charismatic Willie Ryan comes in for the mount.

Peslier teams up with Cloudings (12-1) for owner Sheikh Mohammed and trainer Andre Fabre. The colt won the Prix Lupin but neither owner nor trainer has won the Epsom classic previously and it is 21 years since any horse from France won the Derby.

Fahris (14-1) represents Newmarket trainer Ben Hanbury who will be saddling his first Derby runner. The horse recovered from a sinus problem to win a decent race at Newmarket in April but the Derby is a much tougher, rougher, race.
Best of the rest may be Bold Demand (20-1), the mount of Frankie Dettori and running in the blue Godolphin colours.
The Godolphin operation has been struggling in recent weeks but Bold Demand won the race which Shantou took before finishing third last year and holds similar each-way prospects.
Top trainer Henry Cecil is without a Derby runner but in Friday's Oaks, the fillies' middle-distance classic, he saddles the first two in the betting, Reams Of Verse (4-6) and Yashmak (6-1).
Stable jockey Kieren Fallon has been cleared to ride Reams Of Verse after a 10-day ban picked up in Italy was postponed until June 22.
Yashmak will be ridden by Kinane although if the ground is not in her favour the filly may race instead in the French Oaks.
Friday's Epsom card also features the group one Coronation Cup where Singspiel is poised to add to his impressive list of international big race successes.
